introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. 0796 Information and Communication Technologies 2 (Paper 2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer any SIX questions. All questions carry 17 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You will be scored on your ability to use good English, to organize information clearly and to use specialist vocabulary where appropriate. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is modularisation in programming? (1 mark)

(b) State TWO advantages of modularisation. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Modularisation (1 mark)**

Modularisation is the technique of **breaking a large program (or problem) into smaller, self-contained parts called modules** (procedures, functions, subroutines), **each doing one specific task**, which are written separately and then combined to form the complete program.

**(b) Two advantages (2 marks)**

- **Easier team work and design**: different programmers can write different modules at the same time, and each module is simpler to understand.
- **Easier testing, debugging and maintenance**: each module can be **tested alone**, an error is located quickly and a change is made in one place only.
- (Also acceptable: a module can be **reused** many times in the same or in other programs, which shortens the program and saves time.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Almost all organizations have computer-based information system.

(a) Identify the major components of a computer information system. (3 marks)

(b) Give TWO advantages of an information system to a business organisation. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Major components (3 marks)**

A computer-based information system has five main components:

1. **Hardware**: the computers, storage, input/output devices and network equipment.
2. **Software**: the system software and the application programs that process the data.
3. **Data** (the database): the facts that are collected, stored and turned into information.
4. **People**: the users, the analysts, programmers and operators who run the system.
5. **Procedures**: the rules and instructions that say how the data are collected, processed, backed up and used.

(Three correctly described components earn the marks; the communication network is sometimes added as a sixth.)

**(b) Two advantages to a business (2 marks)**

- It gives **accurate information quickly**, so **managers take better and faster decisions**.
- It **reduces costs and paperwork** (fast processing, less storage space, fewer errors) and **improves communication and co-ordination between departments and with customers**, which gives the firm an advantage over its competitors.

questions.enonce_markdown: The process of downloading a file from the Internet was interrupted. Give TWO possible reasons for this interruption. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Two possible reasons (2 marks)**

- The **Internet connection was lost or became too weak** (network failure, poor signal, congestion, the data bundle ran out).
- A **power cut** or a computer/browser crash happened, or the **server hosting the file went down or removed the file**.
- (Other acceptable reasons: **not enough disk space** on the computer, the download was **blocked by a firewall or antivirus**, the **time-out** of the connection, or the user **cancelled** it.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
A software development schedule is shown in the table below.

| Task | Duration (working days) | Predecessor(s) |
|---|---|---|
| A | 5 | ------ |
| B | 15 | A |
| C | 25 | A |
| D | 15 | B |
| E | 30 | B |
| F | 10 | C, D |
| G | 10 | E, F |
| H | 5 | G |
| I | 5 | H |

(a) Draw the GANTT chart for this project. (3 marks)

(b) State and explain one other management tool that can be used in managing this project (2 marks)

(c) Determine the critical path of this project. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Gantt chart (3 marks)**

Each task is drawn as a **horizontal bar on a time scale**, starting at its **earliest start**, which is the largest finish time of its predecessors. Task A starts at day 0; B and C start when A finishes; D and E start when B finishes; F needs C **and** D; G needs E **and** F; H needs G; I needs H.

| Task | Duration | Earliest start | Earliest finish | Predecessor(s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 5 | 0 | 5 | none |
| B | 15 | 5 | 20 | A |
| C | 25 | 5 | 30 | A |
| D | 15 | 20 | 35 | B |
| E | 30 | 20 | 50 | B |
| F | 10 | 35 | 45 | C, D |
| G | 10 | 50 | 60 | E, F |
| H | 5 | 60 | 65 | G |
| I | 5 | 65 | 70 | H |

The chart (one block = 5 working days; `=` marks the tasks of the critical path, `#` the other tasks):

```text
Task | 0  5  10 15 20 25 30 35 40 45 50 55 60 65 70 (day)
A    | == 
B    |    ======== 
C    |    ############## 
D    |             ######## 
E    |             ================= 
F    |                      ##### 
G    |                               ===== 
H    |                                     == 
I    |                                        == 
```

The whole project lasts **70 working days**. The chart must have a title, the tasks on the vertical axis and the time scale (days or weeks) on the horizontal axis.

**(b) Another management tool (2 marks)**

A **PERT chart / network (activity) diagram**: the tasks are drawn as nodes or arrows joined according to their **dependencies**, with their **durations**. From it the manager calculates the **earliest and latest start and finish times**, the **slack (float)** of each task and the **critical path**, so that he knows which tasks must not be delayed and where resources can be moved. (Other acceptable tools: **project management software** such as MS Project, a **work breakdown structure**, a **milestone chart** or a **resource histogram**.)

**(c) Critical path (2 marks)**

The critical path is the **longest path** through the network, which gives the shortest possible time for the project. The three paths are:

- A - C - F - G - H - I: $5 + 25 + 10 + 10 + 5 + 5 = 60$ days
- A - B - D - F - G - H - I: $5 + 15 + 15 + 10 + 10 + 5 + 5 = 65$ days
- A - B - E - G - H - I: $5 + 15 + 30 + 10 + 5 + 5 = 70$ days

**The critical path is A - B - E - G - H - I, of 70 working days.** These tasks have **zero slack**: any delay on one of them delays the whole project (slack of C = 10 days, D = 5 days, F = 5 days).
